concepts.title: Surface Area of Combination of Solids
concepts.definition: The surface area of a combination of solids is the sum of the curved/lateral surface areas of the individual solids, excluding the areas of any faces that are joined together.
concepts.formula: TSA(combination) = sum of CSA of visible parts
concepts.key_idea: When two solids are joined, the common face is not exposed and its area is excluded from the total surface area calculation.
question_patterns: find surface area of a combination of cylinder and cone
find surface area of a hemisphere surmounted on a cylinder
find surface area of a cone on a cylinder toy
find total surface area of a solid made of two shapes
find curved surface area of a combined solid

solution_steps.explain: Note each exposed part and compute its curved area from its own formula.
Total curved area is the sum over the visible parts.

worked_examples.question: A wooden toy is made by mounting a cone of height 2 cm on a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. Find the total surface area (use pi = 3.14).
A hemisphere of radius 4 cm is surmounted on a cylinder of radius 4 cm and height 7 cm. Find the total surface area.

exercises.question: A solid is in the shape of a cone standing on a hemisphere with both radii 5 cm and cone height 12 cm. Find the total surface area.

concepts.title: Volume of Combination of Solids
concepts.definition: The volume of a combination of solids is the sum of the volumes of the individual component solids.
concepts.key_idea: Unlike surface area, volume is always additive -- no faces are excluded when solids are combined.
question_patterns: find volume of a solid made of cylinder and cone
find volume of a hemisphere on a cylinder
find volume of a combined solid toy
find volume of a capsule shaped solid
find volume of a solid consisting of cone and hemisphere

solution_steps.explain: Break it into standard solids and compute each volume with its own formula.
Total volume is the sum of the part volumes.

concepts.title: Conversion of Solid from One Shape to Another
concepts.definition: When a solid is converted (melted and recast) from one shape to another, its volume remains constant; only the shape changes.
concepts.key_idea: Conservation of volume: the volume before and after recasting is equal; use this to find unknown dimensions.
question_patterns: a metallic sphere is melted and recast into a cylinder find the height
a cone is melted and recast into smaller spheres find number of spheres
a cylinder is recast into a cone find the height of the cone
a solid is converted from one shape to another find new dimension
metal is melted and recast into wire find length of wire

solution_steps.explain: Use the original solid's volume formula from its dimensions.
Write the new shape's volume expression in terms of the unknown.
Set the two expressions equal and solve for the unknown dimension.

concepts.title: Surface Area of Frustum of a Cone
concepts.definition: A frustum of a cone is the portion of the cone between two parallel planes cutting it. Its total surface area includes the curved surface area plus the two circular base areas.
concepts.key_idea: The curved surface area of a frustum uses the slant height l and the two radii r1 and r2; add both circular ends for total surface area.
question_patterns: find the total surface area of a frustum of a cone given r1, r2 and height
calculate the TSA of a bucket shaped frustum
what is the total surface area when both radii and the height are known
determine the frustum total surface area from pi (r1 + r2) l plus the end circles
compute the total area of the frustum surface including both circular ends
how much total surface does the frustum shaped container have

solution_steps.explain: csa = pi x (r1 + r2) x l.
TSA = csa + pi r1^2 + pi r2^2.
solution_steps.compute: tsa = csa + pi * r1 ** 2 + pi * r2 ** 2

concepts.title: Volume of Frustum of a Cone
concepts.definition: The volume of a frustum of a cone is one-third of pi times the height times the sum of the squares of the two radii plus the product of the two radii.
concepts.key_idea: The frustum volume formula combines the areas of both circular ends and their geometric mean, scaled by height and one-third pi.

concepts.title: Slant Height of Frustum of a Cone
concepts.definition: The slant height of a frustum of a cone is the distance along the lateral surface between the two circular edges; it is derived from the Pythagorean theorem.
concepts.key_idea: The slant height forms the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the height and the difference of the two radii as the other two sides.
question_patterns: find the slant height of a frustum of a cone

solution_steps.explain: Take the absolute difference of the two radii.
l = sqrt(h^2 + diff^2).

concepts.title: Word Problems on Volume Conversion
concepts.definition: Volume conversion word problems involve melting, recasting, or reshaping solids from one form to another, where the total volume is conserved and used to find an unknown quantity.
concepts.key_idea: The key principle is conservation of volume; set the volume of the original solid equal to the volume of the new shape and solve for the unknown.

solution_steps.explain: Write the melting solid's volume from its dimensions.
Set it equal to the recast shape's volume expression.
Number of pieces, wire length or new height follows from the equality.
